summary: Zurich's city executive proposed a pricier resident parking card in 2020, withdrew it after voters approved a transport master plan calling for fewer blue-zone spaces in November 2021, and voters approved a weight-based resident card in September 2025; in June 2026 voters rejected an initiative to protect parking-space numbers, and the 1990s parking compromise had been ended in 2021. Since early 2026 the city has run its ten municipal garages itself, and in April 2026 it said Parking Zürich AG could now be formally dissolved. Demand-side events include the pandemic drop in traffic in 2020-2021 and the closure of the Jelmoli department store in February 2025.

items.text: The city executive proposed a revised parking-card ordinance, to be decided by the city parliament, that would raise the annual blue-zone resident card from CHF 300 to CHF 780. Regular overnight parking on public streets, previously free, would be treated like daytime long-stay parking and become chargeable.
items.source_title: Parkieren in Zürich soll neu geregelt werden

items.text: The city closed Parkhaus Central at Seilergraben, its smallest municipal garage with 36 spaces, because modernising it would have been too expensive. The 30 spaces counted under the historic parking compromise were moved to the nearby Parkhaus Urania.

On 28 November 2021, voters approved a new municipal transport master plan stating that blue-zone parking spaces should be reduced. The city then withdrew its 2020 parking-card proposal so that it could draft a revised ordinance.

In a first reading, the city parliament backed a parking-card ordinance with fees based on vehicle weight: 35-45 Rappen per kg for fossil-fuel cars and 30-40 Rappen per kg for zero-emission cars. Only residents without private parking would be eligible. SRF reported the annual fee rising from CHF 300 to CHF 540.
items.source_title: Blaue Zonen - Zürcher Gemeinderat will höhere Parkgebühren für grosse Autos

items.text: Voters approved the new parking-card ordinance with 52.8% yes. According to SRF, blue-zone resident cards will cost about two to three times the previous price, priced by vehicle weight with lower rates for electric cars, and tradespeople get wider parking rights.
items.source_title: Abstimmungen Stadt Zürich - Zürich verbietet Laubbläser

items.text: About 59% of voters rejected the SVP-backed 'Parkplatz-Kompromiss' initiative, which would have allowed public parking to be removed only if the same number stayed available in the district. The report says the city plans to repurpose 9,000-11,000 surface spaces over 10-15 years and that the 1990s parking compromise was ended in 2021.
items.source_title: SVP-Initiative für mehr Parkplätze scheitert in der Stadt Zürich

items.text: Since early 2026, the city's real-estate department (Liegenschaften Stadt Zürich) has run the ten municipal garages and the Zürich Bus Station itself, ending 17 years of outsourcing to Parking Zürich AG (founded 2008). In April 2026 the city said the company could now be formally dissolved, and that nothing changes for customers.
The city parliament approved a Green Party postulate on converting municipal parking garages into housing. The motoring club ACS Zürich, which reported the decision, opposed it.
items.source_title: ACS Zürich verurteilt Gemeinderatsentscheid zum Abbau von Parkhäusern – Schlag gegen die Mobilität und den Wirtschaftsstandort

items.text: Cantonal MPs stated that the University of Zurich raised its parking fees, including at the Irchel garage, by 70-150% for 2023. The cantonal government's reply says the Irchel renovation cost about CHF 25.6 million, occupancy is about 70%, and 220 of 994 long-term rental contracts were cancelled by end of January 2023, not all because of the fee increase.
items.source_title: Anfrage (Erhöhung Tarife auf den Parkplätzen und im Parkhaus der Universität Zürich UZH)

items.text: Six months after the city enabled app payment at its parking meters, about 10% of on-street parking revenue came through apps (505,000 transactions, CHF 1.4 million). Three providers were used: Parkingpay, EasyPark and ParkNow.
items.source_title: Jeder zehnte Franken Parkgebühr fliesst in Zürich per App

items.text: Blick reported that Zurich had about 120 public charging stations, or roughly one per 41 electric cars. It also reported that ewz planned to add more than 20 stations in 2021.
items.source_title: Eine Ladestation für 41 E-Autos: Zürich geht der Pfuus aus

items.text: In a TCS test of EV charging in garages, Zurich scored best of the cities tested, with Hohe Promenade, Urania, Messe Zürich and Opéra assessed. Charging at Opéra cost 28 Rappen per kWh but required the operator's own app.
items.source_title: Elektroauto-Ladestationen in Parkhäusern: Tops und Flops

items.text: The city reported that total traffic fell sharply in the pandemic years 2020 and 2021, with use shifting from public transport towards walking, cycling and cars. By the end of 2022, public transport ridership was almost back to end-2019 levels and cycling counts were at record highs.
items.source_title: Modalsplit der Stadt Zürich: Geprägt von der Pandemie

items.text: The Jelmoli department store on Bahnhofstrasse closed for good. Owner Swiss Prime Site cited changing shopping habits and online retail. Manor is due to occupy three floors of the building from 2027 after renovation.
items.source_title: Ende eines Warenhauses - Jelmoli ist Geschichte: traurige Kunden und ein empörter Ex-Chef
